purpose: Stage a real Linux build, bounded HIA component replacement, complete source/configuration admission and subsequent system comparison without converting any partial success into a whole-kernel or NDU-gain claim.

linux.verification_rule: Record downloaded archive bytes and hash, signed tag/commit linkage and the actual signature-verification method separately. A published checksum or remote signature receipt is not a claim of local GPG verification.

baseline.configuration_rule: Freeze the resolved full .config after the registered boot overlay; retain all differences and require the same configuration/toolchain for matched build comparisons except explicit component/controller switches.
baseline.execution: QEMU TCG guest; correctness and bounded boot smoke only, not bare-metal performance qualification
baseline.raw_evidence_rule: Replay the bound original serial stream; require all 14 unique check identities, complete/shutdown ordering, actual QEMU termination and kernel power-down. Bind the exact image, initramfs and guest program, QEMU/BIOS/argv/run identity, build command and resolved configuration. Summary PASS labels or totals alone are insufficient.
not_established: all Linux selftests or all KUnit tests
SMP race freedom from CPU count alone

denominators.whole_archive: All regular files and symlink targets in the frozen upstream archive, including inactive architectures, tests, tools, build files and documentation; bind a complete gzip JSONL manifest.
denominators.archive_custody: A source manifest alone inventories its observed directory; it does not prove membership in the named release archive. A stock build claim additionally requires the manifest's per-file path/type/bytes/hash and per-symlink path/type/target to equal the archive-verified baseline before/after snapshots. A changed extraction or repaired symlink needs new immutable evidence; do not mix it with an older manifest even when file counts agree.
denominators.source_files_total: A suffix-classified file count only. It is not a semantic rewrite denominator: linker scripts, device trees, Kconfig and generators can be in other.
denominators.active_compile_units: Every original target-C compilation-database entry for one resolved configuration, including duplicates for distinct commands/objects; this is not the whole Kbuild denominator.
denominators.target_c_subset: Keep the original full gen_compile_commands database unchanged. Bind a separately selected target database and original indices, choosing only entries whose file suffix is .c and whose original arguments contain -D__KERNEL__. Preserve each selected entry exactly and retain host/unknown entries in the full database and a separate intake ledger. Selection is an accounting boundary, not permission to rewrite flags or evidence of whole-Kbuild coverage.
denominators.whole_kbuild: Requires a separate complete accounting of target C, assembly, Rust, generated inputs, link inputs and modules; distinguish host build tools. It is not established by a C compilation database.
denominators.functions_and_symbols: Unknown until actually parsed and mapped. Never infer function count from source-file count; nm/System.map omit inlined, eliminated and other source-level entities. Preserve source-to-HIA-to-object-to-linked-image mappings and separate runtime execution evidence.
denominators.runtime: Report actually reached replacement bodies and calls separately from compiled objects, boot success, available symbols and untaken fallback paths.
denominators.missing_rule: Planned failed, rejected, skipped and not-run entries remain in the denominator with a reason. No dropping unsupported flags, files, architectures, tests or controller cells after seeing outcomes.

accepted_evidence.translation_intake_capability: This v1 intake exercises existing C/Hepta admission; it does not emit a complete HIA kernel. Admitted GNU-C command intake, Hepta/Rust output or sharded command acceptance cannot be promoted to source-qualified HIA kernel translation.
accepted_evidence.component_capability: A source-bound HIA body, retained assembly bridge and mixed-image guest witness can establish only the named component replacement. Original C/assembly/64-bit fallbacks remain explicit; no source/TU/global percentage is inferred from one body. Completed runtime-input driver calls are labeled as such, not presented as counters of natural whole-system traffic. __x86_return_thunk is required exactly when the bound CONFIG_MITIGATION_RETHUNK=y configuration requires it; hosted allocator/abort runtimes are not permitted. Replay Core/LLVM/object admission and actual linked arithmetic bytes and bridge target, then independently replay the matching mixed boot report; a bound but uninterpreted JSON label is insufficient.

claims.stock_kernel_built: A passing full frozen-config stock Kbuild and bound kernel image.
claims.stock_kernel_booted: The matching image completes every registered guest check and the host-observed boot/exit gate.
claims.hia_component_replacement_executed: A qualified HIA object and explicit routing are bound to a mixed kernel image, independent output checks and a guest report showing positive calls to the named HIA replacement.
claims.hia_whole_config_translated: Requires complete whole-Kbuild implementation coverage with explicit retained/trusted components, source and ABI obligations; unavailable from the present intake/component evidence schemas.
claims.hia_kernel_booted: Reserved for a whole-config HIA kernel that satisfies the previous claim and its registered boot/correctness contract; a mixed component image does not satisfy this claim.
claims.whole_source_rewrite_established: Requires a registered architecture/configuration matrix, implementation and build-generation coverage, link/UAPI/hardware admission, not just one config or all .c files.
claims.global_comparison_completed: Requires eligible whole-config HIA images, original Linux controls and the complete prospectively registered real-system comparison. No bootable HIA kernel means NOT_RUN.
claims.ndu_unique_gain_established: Requires favorable held-out end-to-end net results against the strongest fair ordinary controls with uncertainty and costs included; no superiority is assumed.

comparison.fairness: All adaptive HIA controls have the same observation interface, candidate permissions, forecast inputs and compute caps, and are scored by one external objective. Their declared internal planning objectives may differ. Original Linux retains its native algorithms, including existing adaptivity. Use matched static translation controls to separate language/code-generation effects from controller effects.
comparison.coupling: CPU, memory, I/O and synchronization demands share real resources. A joint controller pays for coordination, stale observations, computation, admission and switching; independent per-subsystem maxima are not a whole-system optimum. Runtime computation must consume actual CPU/memory/time and affect feasibility.
comparison.holdout: Freeze data/model/configuration/candidates and choices before held-out execution; record all repeats, invalidations and failures. Future requests, validation outcomes and realized future costs are never passed to online controllers.
comparison.oracle: A small bounded projection may have an exact oracle. It is labeled separately and cannot be used as free future information or as a full Linux optimum.
comparison.results: Retain every planned arm/workload/repeat cell with PASS, FAIL, SKIP or NOT_RUN and reasons. Correctness failures are not discarded to improve speed. Kernel image, boot and workload outputs must be real; userspace microbenchmarks alone do not establish a kernel rewrite.

version_specific_test_note: The fetched 6.18.60 tools/testing/selftests/Makefile has FORCE_TARGETS but lacks the newer KSFT_BUILD_REPORT documented in latest docs. Use FORCE_TARGETS=1 and an external per-target result ledger on this pinned source. KUnit defaults cover only tests reachable in its minimal config, not all kernel tests.
